# Django porting rules

1. **Read the installed source, not memory.** Django is pinned (`django>=6.1,<6.2`); read
   `.venv/lib/python*/site-packages/django/...` for the exact version (`uv run python -c
   "import django; print(django.__version__)"`). Delegate large reads to `django-researcher`.
2. **Port, don't paraphrase.** Keep the ported function's structure, names and branch order
   so a future diff against upstream is mechanical. Only change what is needed for async:
   replace I/O calls with awaits on our layer; keep pure-Python parts identical.
3. **Attribute every port** with a header comment:
   `# Ported from django/db/models/query.py::prefetch_one_level @ 6.1.3 - <what changed>`.
4. **Reuse helpers only after an I/O audit** (`RelatedPopulator`, `get_converters`), and record
   them in the ledger. "Pure-looking" helpers can hide I/O: `GenericForeignKey.get_prefetch_querysets`
   queries ContentType on a cache miss. Ported orchestration is a sans-I/O generator core
   (ADR-0007), not an `async def` copy.
5. **Import internals only in `asyncopation._django`** and ledger every one in `docs/django-api-ledger.toml` (`module`, `names`,
   `used_by` (the real consumers), `reason`, `verified_against`). The guard rejects unknown internals (A201),
   private Django imports outside `_django` (A203) and stale entries (A202: an `[[internal]]` item not
   imported under `_django`, an `[[attribute]]` never accessed, a `ported` entry whose `used_by` file is missing or has no
   `# Ported from django/<module path>.py` comment). Add `signatures = { "Name.method" = "<str(inspect.signature)>" }`
   (dotted keys must be quoted) for callables whose signature you depend on, mark code you only port and
   never import (the MySQL backend) `ported = true`, and register every Django private attribute you access
   directly, inside `_django` or not (`qs._fetch_mode`), as an `[[attribute]]` (`owner`, `names`, `used_by`,
   `reason`, `verified_against`); the drift test (`tests/unit/django_drift`) checks all of it against installed Django.
   The guard cannot detect private attribute access - arch review does.
   A third-party package whose behaviour we depend on at run time without importing it (asgiref
   `Local`, ADR-0008) is a `[[dependency]]` row (`package`, `names` below the package, `used_by`,
   `reason`, `verified_against` = an exact `X.Y.Z`, one row per package). A202 does not apply
   (nothing is imported); the drift test requires the installed version to **equal**
   `verified_against` and pyproject to carry a requirement for the package that admits it: when the lock moves, re-read
   the pinned behaviour tests, then update `verified_against`.
6. **Differential test every port** against the sync implementation on all backends.
7. The `django-main` CI canary runs `tests/unit/django_drift tests/unit/compile -m "not django_pin"` (with mysqlclient installed and `ASYNCOPATION_REQUIRE_MYSQLDB=1`, so the MySQL wrapper drift tests cannot skip) and `tests/integration` against Django main. When it breaks, update ports and bump `verified_against`. (The `django_pin` tests assert the pinned minor and are skipped there; `uv run --no-sync` is required, a re-sync would restore the locked Django.)
